title: Asymmetric prefix decay savings scenarios (May 2026)
summary: Exploratory workbook modeling asymmetric prefix (KV) decay across user cohorts. We compare short- vs long-half-life behavior, asymmetric decay across cohorts, and the downstream cost impact per 1M requests. This is intended as a proofof-concept to inform caching policy recommendations (per-cohort TTL, aggressive prefetch for high-tenure users, and lossy compression trade-offs). Key finding: targeted warm-starts for ~20% of requests (high-tenure cohort) capture ~60–75% of practical savings without a cluster-wide prefix footprint increase.
assumptions: Unit token cost = $0.00025 (weighted average across model family). Average tokens_per_request = 320 (prompt+response). Baseline KV/prefix disabled hit rate = 2–5% depending on cohort. 'Warmed' policy means per-cohort half-life tuning + conservative prefetch; warmed_hit_rate estimates are empirical approximations from telemetry samples. Cache storage and eviction overheads are modeled separately; this sheet focuses on token-serving delta only. Monthly volume baseline = 1,000,000 requests for normalized savings. Latency and SLA impact not included in dollar figures. All percentages rounded to nearest integer for readability.
cell_notes: Columns explained: tokens_served_without_cache = tokens_per_request (no token-level saving). tokens_served_with_cache = tokens_per_request * (1 - warmed_hit_rate) + (tokens_per_request * warmed_hit_rate * residual_response_fraction). We approximate residual_response_fraction = avg_response_tokens / tokens_per_request for warm hits to account for partial token savings (prefix saves prompt tokens and some repeated response tokens). Percent cost reduction is computed on overall tokens delta. Rows are normalized to 1M requests for monthly savings estimates.
conclusion: A small subset of traffic (high-tenure cohort) provides outsized cache returns because of long effective prefix half-life. A policy that targets ~15–25% of requests for stronger warming/persistent prefixes is cost-effective: it recovers ~60%+ of total token savings while only increasing prefix store footprint modestly. Lossy prefetching (trimmed prefix representation) is a middle-ground that preserves most hitrate without linear storage growth.
recommended_actions: Pilot per-cohort prefix half-life: set default half-life=3 requests, persistent for cohort tagged as high-tenure with half-life=12+, monitor hit and footprint weekly (30-day pilot)
Implement lossy prefix encoding for regular users (compress vectorized prefix or hashed-prefix buckets) and measure effective warmed_hit_rate vs storage cost tradeoff over 2 weeks
Add telemetry labels to capture "cohort_age" and "recent-frequency" to feed the next optimization iteration
Run A/B comparing conservative warming (prefetch on warm path) vs aggressive warming (background prefetch) for high-tenure cohort to measure latency/SLA regressions
